html:
The first independent Muslim kingdom of the Deccan in south-central India, ruling from 1347 until it broke into the five Deccan sultanates in the early 1500s.

It began when nobles in the Deccan rebelled against Muhammad bin Tughluq of the Delhi Sultanate and chose one of their own, Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah, as king. The first capital was Gulbarga. In the 1420s it moved to Bidar.

The sultans fought the Hindu kingdom of Vijayanagara to the south again and again, mostly over the rich land between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers. At court, nobles from Persia, Arabia and Central Asia competed with Deccan-born Muslims, and this feud weakened the state.

Its greatest minister was Mahmud Gawan, a Persian merchant who reformed the army and finances and built a large madrasa in Bidar in 1472. The Russian merchant Afanasy Nikitin visited Bidar in these years and left a description of it (Afanasy Nikitin in India). Mahmud Gawan was executed in 1481 on a forged charge, and the kingdom fell apart. Its provincial governors made themselves kings in Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Berar and Golconda, and the last Bahmani sultans were puppets in Bidar until 1527.
sum: The first independent Muslim kingdom of the Deccan in south-central India, ruling from 1347 until it broke into the five Deccan sultanates in the early 1500s.
